source_context_translations.translation: The Way that can be spoken of is not the constant Way; the name that can be named is not the constant name.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A physical route or track for travel from one place to another.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Used for an actual way of passage.
Sentence Translations (English): He traveled along the mountain path and reached the outer walls at dusk.
At the fork ahead, he followed the right-hand road.
The cart broke down in the mud, so he abandoned it and walked on the path.
The people blocked the road, and travelers became scarce.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A way of doing something, especially a practical procedure, technique, or means for achieving a result.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Focuses on the practical means or procedure, not on a doctrine or moral path.
Sentence Translations (English): There is a method for governing a state, and it does not lie in harsh punishments.
In learning calligraphy, one should grasp the method, not merely copy the form.
The means to remedy abuses is first to set the root right.
If a craftsman wants to do fine work, he must practice the method.
Sentences: 學書貴得其道，不徒摹形。

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To speak, state, or express in words.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): A plain verbal act of saying or describing, often with an object or quoted content.
Sentence Translations (English): The master stated the matter, and all listened to him.
I do not dare to speak of the details.
The historian stated its faults plainly and did not conceal them.
When the guest came to ask, the host slowly described what he had heard.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The ultimate, indefinable principle or source that underlies reality and cannot be fully expressed in words.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In this context, it names what can be followed or spoken about only provisionally, not a concrete road or an ordinary method.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text as transmitted in the Wang Bi recension
